div.note: The Latin is the Quadripartitus; Liebermann's Old English is from X (Oxford, Bodleian, Junius 121, f. 13b, written at Worcester c. 1065). In OE the text survives only as a chapter in the middle of the so-called Polity (a compilation of c. 1027–60), but was perhaps originally separate, as the Quadripartitus had it. Liebermann dates it c. 1000–1050 and gives the German title in brackets as his own.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.1000–1050; ??(Whitelock); 1002x1008 (Rabin)”, now “c.1000–1050 (Liebermann); 1002×1008 (Rabin)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (column heads, read twice), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “Q 477; X 477; German 477”; 16 rows of Episc)
